text:
Victor Hedman has four goals in 21 games, already more than the one he scored in 33 games last season, and that's the warning label. He's shooting 19% (2% a year ago) on 1.3 expected goals. The chances are real; that finishing rate rarely lasts. He's also pointless in seven straight, on 2.7 expected points.

The usage tells a story too. Hedman is playing 15.8 minutes a night on the season but that number has climbed to nearly 18 over the last 10 games. Tampa takes 51% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, 7.5 points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey notes his teammates rank in the 92nd percentile by impact and had him around replacement level last season.

What's still elite is the passing. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him at 6.4 primary shot assists per 60 (92nd percentile among defensemen) and breaking the puck out with possession 52% of the time. The Norris winner and Conn Smythe winner is 35 and coming off a 33-game season; the passing is the part of his game to watch while the shooting comes back to earth.
